ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a simple series circuit, with an ammeter/galvanometer G on the left and a resistor R on the right; the two are connected in series on the same branch and connected across the two ends of the applied voltage U. The figure also marks the current flowing through the meter movement as I_g. Reasoning: At full deflection, the circuit current equals the full-deflection current of the meter movement, I_g = 100 μA. The applied voltage U = 10 V, so the total resistance required for the whole series circuit is R_total = U / I_g = 10 V / 100 μA = 10 / 0.0001 Ω = 100000 Ω = 100 kΩ. The meter movement's own internal resistance r_g = 1 kΩ, and R is in series with the meter movement, so the external series resistor R = R_total - r_g = 100 kΩ - 1 kΩ = 99 kΩ.
